subject: CareLoom discovery — integration fit & SLO matrix
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Emily Zhao <emily@careloom.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: CareLoom discovery — integration fit & SLO matrix

Hi Emily (and Rajiv),

Thanks again for taking the 45-minute discovery with us today — great conversation. Below is a concise synthesis of the call, the pain we heard, and proposed next steps so we can get to a scoped pilot quickly. Please flag anything we've mis-captured.

High-level summary
- Primary pain: CareLoom is seeing significant triage latency and a high volume of false positives from the current NLU stack when handling insurance/eligibility questions. This increases manual review and slows patient intake.
- Goal: Reduce average triage handling time by ~40% and lower manual-review rate by half within the pilot (6–8 weeks).
- Key constraints: PHI must remain in their VPC for production-only workloads; initial pilot can use pseudonymized records but needs strict audit logs.

Integration & product fit notes (what we discussed)
- Embeddings + rerank: You prefer an embeddings-first retrieval with Redwood reranking to reduce hallucinations in short-form clinical Q/A.
- Streaming / function calling: CareLoom wants streaming token-level responses for an interactive triage UI and function-calls to pass structured insurance-check results back into their system.
- SDK changes: Minimal – we recommended integrating the Redwood JS SDK for streaming (client) and a small server-side adaptor to call their eligibility API via function-calls.
- Structured outputs: We suggested a constrained JSON proto for insurance decisions (fields: decision, confidence, reason_codes[]) to make downstream automation deterministic.

Security/compliance checkpoint
- Redwood Private (VPC) is the intended production path. For pilot we can run in hosted with pseudonymization and an isolated project. Monica will outline minimal evidence (audit logs, retention policy, SOC2 scope) in a follow-up.

Attachments sent with this email:
- SLO_matrix.xlsx — proposed latency/cost/quality SLO targets for pilot
- integration_diagram.png — sketched adapter flow (Redwood -> function call -> CareLoom eligibility API)

Next steps (requested commitments)
1) Emily/Rajiv: Confirm pilot dataset availability (pseudonymized sample, ~5k records) and a contact for infra (someone who can whitelist IPs).
2) CareLoom: Accept SLO targets or suggest edits (see SLO_matrix.xlsx).
3) Redwood: We will produce a one-page MAP (mutual action plan) with milestones and an initial infra checklist by EOD Monday.

Timing
- Proposed pilot start: week of 7/12 if dataset and infra access are ready.

If that all looks right I’ll loop Ben to draft pricing options for a 6–8 week pilot and Monica will follow up on compliance artifacts.

Thanks — enjoyed the discussion.

—
Logan Wright
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Sounds good on MAP and dates. I’ll confirm infra contact (cc’ing Rajiv) by Monday. Also, Ben — happy to see an estimate for pilot pricing.

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Subject: CareLoom — Pilot MAP & next steps

Emily — following up with the mutual action plan and an initial pilot estimate. Attached is a short MAP PDF and the SLO/X checklist we discussed.

Pilot estimate (6 weeks) — banded
- Hosted isolated pilot: $18k (reduced throughput SLA, hosted project w/ pseudonymized data)
- Dedicated pilot (recommended for accurate latency guarantees): $28k (isolated GPU pool for duration)

Proposed MAP (high level)
1) Week 0 (7/5): CareLoom provides pseudonymized sample dataset (~6k records) + infra contact to whitelist Redwood egress.
2) Week 1 (7/12): Initial integration sprint — Redwood delivers SDK adaptor and function-call example; CareLoom starts local adapter testing.
3) Weeks 2–4 (7/19–8/9): Tuning & rerank pass, automated test suite on sample set, quality acceptance (target: 40% triage time reduction).
4) Weeks 5–6 (8/9–8/23): Pilot run on live traffic (pseudonymized or private path as agreed), SLO measurement, and final ops handoff.

Deliverables we’ll provide by 7/5:
- MAP PDF (attached)
- Example audit log for hosted vs. private (Monica will send)
- Integration diagram and SDK example repo link

Attachments: CareLoom_MAP.pdf (PDF, 45KB), SLO_matrix.xlsx (Excel, 14KB)
Related links: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/678912345 (CareLoom opportunity)

If this matches your expectations we’ll open a pilot PO template and share a statement of work. Open to a quick 20-minute call early next week to walk the MAP with your infra/security folks.

Thanks,
Ben
